vsaq.answer: A living organism is a self-replicating, evolving and self-regulating system capable of responding to external stimuli.

vsaq.question: Define Five-kingdom classification.
vsaq.answer: R. H. Whittaker classified organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia using cell type, organisation, nutrition, reproduction and phylogeny.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Three-domain system?
vsaq.answer: Carl Woese recognised Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya mainly from ribosomal RNA and molecular differences.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Archaebacteria.
vsaq.answer: Archaea have ether-linked membrane lipids and distinctive cell walls, enabling many to live in extreme habitats.

vsaq.question: Define Eubacteria.
vsaq.answer: Eubacteria are true prokaryotes with peptidoglycan walls; they may be autotrophic or heterotrophic.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Cyanobacteria?
vsaq.answer: Cyanobacteria are oxygenic photosynthetic prokaryotes; heterocysts in forms such as Nostoc fix atmospheric nitrogen.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Mycoplasma.
vsaq.answer: Mycoplasmas are the smallest self-replicating cells and lack a cell wall, so their shape is variable.

vsaq.question: Define Protista.
vsaq.answer: Protista contains mostly unicellular eukaryotes, including chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Diatoms?
vsaq.answer: Diatoms have siliceous, two-piece walls called frustules; accumulated walls form diatomaceous earth.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Dinoflagellates.
vsaq.answer: Dinoflagellates possess two unequal flagella; rapid multiplication of some marine species causes red tides.

vsaq.question: Define Euglenoids.
vsaq.answer: Euglenoids lack a cell wall, possess a protein-rich pellicle and can shift between autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Fungi?
vsaq.answer: Fungi are absorptive heterotrophs with chitinous walls; their hyphae form a mycelium and reproduce by spores.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Fungal classes.
vsaq.answer: Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes and Deuteromycetes are distinguished mainly by mycelium and sexual spores.

vsaq.question: Define Virus.
vsaq.answer: A virus is an acellular nucleoprotein particle that multiplies only inside a living host cell.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Viroid and prion?
vsaq.answer: A viroid is naked infectious RNA, whereas a prion is an infectious misfolded protein.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Lichen.
vsaq.answer: A lichen is a mutualistic association in which an alga supplies food and a fungus provides shelter, water and minerals.

vsaq.question: Define Botany.
vsaq.answer: Botany is the scientific study of plants, including their structure, function, diversity, heredity, ecology and uses.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Theophrastus?
vsaq.answer: Theophrastus is called the Father of Botany because his works Historia Plantarum and De Causis Plantarum systematically described plants.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Indian botany.
vsaq.answer: Ancient Indian works such as Vrikshayurveda recorded plant classification, cultivation, diseases and medicinal uses.

vsaq.question: Define Morphology.
vsaq.answer: Plant morphology studies the external form and visible organs of plants.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Anatomy?
vsaq.answer: Plant anatomy studies internal organisation of cells, tissues and organs.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Taxonomy.
vsaq.answer: Plant taxonomy identifies, names and classifies plants using diagnostic characters.

vsaq.question: Define Cytology.
vsaq.answer: Cytology studies plant cells, their organelles, chromosomes and division.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Embryology?
vsaq.answer: Plant embryology examines formation and development of gametes, embryo and seed.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Physiology.
vsaq.answer: Plant physiology explains functions such as absorption, transport, photosynthesis, respiration and growth.

vsaq.question: Define Genetics.
vsaq.answer: Plant genetics studies inheritance, variation and the expression of genes in plants.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Ecology?
vsaq.answer: Plant ecology examines relationships of plants with one another and with their physical environment.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Palaeobotany.
vsaq.answer: Palaeobotany reconstructs the history and evolution of plants from fossils.

vsaq.question: Define Economic botany.
vsaq.answer: Economic botany studies plants and plant products used as food, fibre, timber, medicines and industrial raw materials.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Plant pathology?
vsaq.answer: Plant pathology investigates plant diseases, their causes, spread, effects and control.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Biotechnology and scope.
vsaq.answer: Plant biotechnology uses cells, genes and tissue culture to improve crops, conserve germplasm and produce useful compounds.

vsaq.question: Define Meristematic tissue.
vsaq.answer: Meristematic cells actively divide, have dense cytoplasm, prominent nuclei, thin walls and little or no vacuolation.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Apical, intercalary and lateral meristems?
vsaq.answer: Apical and intercalary meristems lengthen organs; lateral meristems increase girth by secondary growth.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Simple permanent tissues.
vsaq.answer: Parenchyma performs storage or photosynthesis, collenchyma gives flexible support, and lignified sclerenchyma gives strength.

vsaq.question: Define Xylem.
vsaq.answer: Xylem conducts water and minerals through tracheids and vessels; fibres support and parenchyma stores food.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Phloem?
vsaq.answer: Phloem transports organic food through sieve elements assisted by companion cells; fibres support and parenchyma stores.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Tissue systems.
vsaq.answer: Epidermal, ground and vascular tissue systems respectively protect, perform basic functions and conduct materials.

vsaq.question: Define Dicot root.
vsaq.answer: A dicot root has radial vascular bundles, exarch xylem, small pith and later develops secondary growth.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Monocot root?
vsaq.answer: A monocot root has many radial xylem bundles, large pith and normally lacks secondary growth.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Dicot stem.
vsaq.answer: A dicot stem has vascular bundles in a ring; bundles are conjoint, collateral and open due to cambium.

vsaq.question: Define Monocot stem.
vsaq.answer: A monocot stem has numerous scattered, closed vascular bundles surrounded by sclerenchymatous bundle sheaths.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Dorsiventral leaf?
vsaq.answer: A dicot leaf has palisade tissue above, spongy tissue below and more stomata on the lower epidermis.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Isobilateral leaf.
vsaq.answer: A monocot leaf has similar surfaces, stomata on both, undifferentiated mesophyll and bulliform cells.

vsaq.question: Define Vascular cambium.
vsaq.answer: Cambial ring produces secondary xylem inward and secondary phloem outward, increasing stem girth.

vsaq.question: What is meant by Cork cambium?
vsaq.answer: Phellogen forms cork outward and secondary cortex inward; lenticels permit gaseous exchange through periderm.

vsaq.question: Write a short note on Wood and annual rings.
vsaq.answer: Seasonal differences create spring wood and autumn wood; one pair forms an annual ring useful in estimating age.
